items.title: Show HN: Plain-Auth an open-source authentication library for Go
items.summary: Hey everyone, I've always loved the simplicity of Go, but the only thing keeping me from switching all of my backends to Go is really one package, and one package only, which is Better-Auth. It's just so easy to use: simple plugin, and start working. It's got everything I need: organizations, teams, billing, social auth, everything. I tried to scour GitHub and the open source community for anything remotely close to it in Go, and I honestly couldn't find anything that was worth it, so I just decided to make it myself. It's an open-source Go package. It is not 100% feature parity with Better-Auth yet, but it's getting there. Would love some feedback. For anyone to try it out, it works with pretty much all of those routers: Chi, Echo, Fiber, Mux and more. Any feedback is greatly appreciated. Oh, and it's also my very first open source repo, so I'm learning as I go.

items.title: Show HN: A free browser backgammon club, gnubg's net under the hood
items.summary: Using Spawn, I've been building The Velvet Point, a rainy-night backgammon club you play in the browser (desktop or phone). You can play the house opponents or real people, and chat at the tables. You will also get analytical (as well as snarky) comments from the AI opponents. Social features, leaderboards (ratings, PR, chips) also baked in. Has a review feature to show the best moves after your move. So no "hint" or tutoring before the move. I think you will learn better when you make a mistake - making a mistake will give your brain the feedback you need to learn better. Uses gnubg's neural nets & bear-off tables in the background, ported to run in the browser. It's open source ( https://github.com/ile/the-velvet-point ). Play here: https://www.spawn.co/@ilkkah/the-velvet-point I'd love feedback. There may be bugs (hopefully just minor ones).

items.title: Show HN: A local-first AI memory for your video footage
items.summary: I'm Ilias, the creator behind Orcah Studio (a local-first knowledge system that will transcribe, perform speaker diarization, analyse frames, and create multi-modal embeddings) using open-weight models Demo video: https://youtu.be/9uUZrayDEgs I built a Docker-first solution, fully open source here: https://github.com/IliasHad/orcah-studio Plus, a desktop app that will be plug-and-play with a richer video indexing pipeline. With integrations with DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, and Adobe Premiere Pro, and MCP tools (over 45 tools). You can even link your videos with your Strava activities and extract camera metadata like ISO, Shutter Speed, Lens Model, and location, if available. You can even do the same in your iPhone videos (index your videos in your videos, sync them with your Mac-indexed videos, so you can search them from your Mac or the other way). (Early alpha for now) And even index videos on your Linux machine (alpha version) and use the macOS application as a client for that machine. The goal is to make your videos indexable, searchable and most importantly, to build a memory from all your videos and connect the dots. Instead of just building a memory for a specific video, we can connect and link between all the videos that you have, without uploading anything to the cloud or paying us a subscription (one-time fee, no subscription fatigue or reminders haha) Here's the macOS app that you can buy and start indexing your videos now: https://orcah.app
